claims.text: Incorporating machine-learning potentials into DFT free-energy studies will improve determination of the solid-to-fluid transition temperature in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Incorporating machine-learning potentials into DFT free-energy studies will improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Incorporating machine-learning potentials into DFT free-energy studies will improve determination of volume change at the solid-to-fluid transition.
Incorporating machine-learning potentials into DFT free-energy studies will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
Machine-learning potentials improve the accuracy of DFT free-energy studies for multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Machine-learning potentials improve the computational efficiency of DFT free-energy studies for multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The improved accuracy and efficiency provided by machine-learning potentials allow better representation of thermodynamic effects around the transition.
The proposed approach can treat both the solid and dense-fluid phases around the transition.
The intended domain is multicomponent high-entropy materials at high temperatures near a solid-to-fluid transition.
Performance should be assessed by comparing DFT free-energy calculations with and without machine-learning potentials on the same multicomponent high-entropy material.
